## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Daddarajātaka* (Ja 438), rendered in modern translation as "The Partridge", is a birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to its opening framework preserved in the tradition, the Buddha related this story while residing at Vulture Peak (Gijjhakūṭa) in connection with Devadatta's ongoing efforts to slay him, beginning with the verse line "Thy harmless offspring" [SuttaCentral]. The text shares its title with two other homonymous birth stories in the collection (Ja 172 and Ja 304), each concerning separate narratives; all passages located in the research dossier address either Ja 172, Ja 304, or incidental lexical and geographical uses of the name *Daddara*.

SuttaCentral records four modern translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus registers no cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora exceeding the match threshold [DharmaNexus].
